subject: general
question: In which of the following years was The Indian Official Language Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1963**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Official Language Act** was passed in **1963**.
 
• The Act provides for the **continued use of English**, in addition to Hindi, for** official purposes** of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament.
 
• This was enacted to address the concerns of non-Hindi speaking states regarding the exclusive use of Hindi for official purposes.
 
• The Act is a crucial part of India's linguistic policy and ensures linguistic diversity is respected in official matters.
 
• The Act has been amended several times to extend the use of English for official purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, includes provisions for the official languages of India.
 
• **Article 343** of the Constitution declares **Hindi in the Devanagari script** as the** official language of the Union**.
 
• The Constitution also provides for the use of **English for official purposes for a period of 15 years** from the date of commencement of the Constitution, after which Parliament could decide on its continued use.
 
• The Indian Official Language Act of 1963 was a result of the constitutional provision and the need to accommodate linguistic diversity in India.
